title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E506 is Euler's commentary on Lagrange's method (Misc. Taurinensia IV, 1766–69) for integrating dx/√X = dy/√Y. Before the elliptic case, Euler warms up (§9 onward) with the rational equation dx/(a+2bx+cx²) = dy/(a+2by+cy²), writing X = a+2bx+cx² and Y = a+2by+cy².

§10: Following Lagrange, both equal ratios are set equal to a common auxiliary differential dt, so dx/dt = X and dy/dt = Y; x and y become functions of a 'time' t. With q = x−y one has dq/dt = X−Y = q(2b + c(x+y)), hence q̇/q = 2b + c(x+y).

§11: Differentiating again with dt constant: ẍ = X'ẋ, so ẍ/ẋ = X' and ÿ/ẏ = Y'. Adding gives ẍ/ẋ + ÿ/ẏ = X'+Y' = 4b + 2c(x+y).

§12: This is exactly 2q̇/q. So d ln ẋ + d ln ẏ = 2 d ln q, which integrates to ẋẏ = C q². Substituting ẋ = X and ẏ = Y eliminates t and gives the complete algebraic integral XY/(x−y)² = C.

Next page: adding b²−ac makes the numerator a perfect square, giving the Möbius/bilinear integral (a+b(x+y)+cxy)/(x−y) = Δ. §14 shows the same trick fails when X is cubic.

The point of the page is pedagogical. It isolates the core of Lagrange's device in the simplest setting: auxiliary time, then logarithmic second derivatives, then comparison with q̇/q. Euler then extends it to the square-root (quartic) case.
errors: Print omission: 'ddx/(dx dt) X'' lacks the '=' sign; it should read ddx/(dx dt) = X'.
Print omission: 'dy/dt Y' near the end lacks '='; it should read dy/dt = Y.
The mathematics is otherwise correct: X−Y = (x−y)(2b+c(x+y)), and the derivation ẋẏ = Cq² is valid. Implicitly X, Y ≠ 0 and x ≠ y.

ideas.what: Introducing an auxiliary parameter t with dx/dt = X, dy/dt = Y, then differentiating a second time to obtain an integrable combination
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange's method / parametrization by a common flow time; finding a first integral of a 2D autonomous system
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (Misc. Taur. IV, 1766–69); Euler's E506 is the known exposition
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1778:II, publ. 1781); the method is Lagrange's

ideas.what: Complete algebraic integral XY/(x−y)² = C of dx/X = dy/Y with X quadratic, equivalent to the bilinear relation (a+b(x+y)+cxy)/(x−y) = const
ideas.modern_name: One-parameter Möbius group preserving a quadratic (invariance of cross-ratio with the two roots); addition law for arctan/log
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (earlier treatments of separated equations, e.g. Institutiones calculi integralis and the papers on the addition theorem)
ideas.where_published: Euler's integral-calculus works on separated equations (exact locus unsure); also E506 §13

deep.surprise_reason: This is a well-known expository paper (E506) on Lagrange's method. The rational warm-up case is classical and correct, and nothing on the page is uncredited or unexplored.
transcription_corrections: 'ddx/(dx dt) X'' should be 'ddx/(dx dt) = X'' (the '=' is missing in the print itself).
'dy/dt Y' should be 'dy/dt = Y' (the '=' is missing in the print).
The page header ') 25 (' is the original pagination of Acta Acad. Imp. Sc. Tom. II P. I; the footer signature 'D' and catchword '§. 13.' are correctly rendered.
